comment: Field maps by hand, for protocols whose whole frame is known: where each field lies in KAT's data word (offset: its lowest bit; bit 0 is the word's last bit) and in the extra word. scripts/site_frames.py finds serial, button and counter by itself; a map here replaces what it found.

Opel Rolling.note: The held frame is 32 bits: `9`, the serial, a check nibble. [The page above](opel_rolling.md#frame-60-bits-15-nibbles) has the mask.

fields.name: Button
fields.note: `A` Unlock, `B` Lock

fields.name: Plain value, masked
fields.note: three fixed nibbles and the 12-bit counter, each nibble plus `r` and some inverted

fields.name: r, inverted
fields.note: the nibble the remote picks for the press

Suzuki TS002.note: The frame is 72 bits: the data word is its first 64, the extra word its last 8.

fields.name: Head
fields.note: `14` in every frame of the recorded remote

fields.name: Button
fields.note: `01` Lock, `02` Unlock; `20` is added while held

fields.name: Code
fields.note: with the extra word, 32 bits: the inverted counter byte in four pairs, and the ID rotated by it

Renault 1-Button.note: The frame is 70 bits; with two 0 bits in front it is nine bytes: the data word holds the first eight, the extra word the ninth.

fields.name: Start
fields.note: two 0 bits of the lead and `11`

fields.name: Check
fields.note: the XOR of the nine bytes is 0

Volvo S40.note: The frame is 64 bits, all in the data word; each byte goes out LSB first. The Serial column shows `p1..p4`, the Counter `n`; `p5` and `p6` are on [the page above](volvo_s40.md#frame-64-bits).

fields.name: Sum
fields.note: `n + p1 + … + p6` (mod 256); when it is odd the other seven bytes come backwards

fields.name: Counter and six bytes
fields.note: `n`, then `p1 ^ n` … `p6 ^ n`; `n` first when the sum is even, last when it is odd

fields.name: Head
fields.note: `CE` in every frame of the recorded key

fields.name: Button
fields.note: `C` Unlock, `3` Lock

fields.name: Code
fields.note: changes with every press

PSA 2-Button.note: The frame is 76 bits: the extra word is its first 12, the data word its last 64.

fields.name: UID (obfuscated)
fields.note: the 32-bit fob ID on the wire, each byte XORed with `m` = byte4 ^ byte5 ^ byte6; the Serial column shows it undone

fields.name: Register
fields.note: the 24-bit LFSR state; advances 23 ticks every press

fields.name: Button
fields.note: `1` Unlock, `2` Lock

VW-1.note: The frame is 60 bits, all in the data word, sent LSB-first within each byte. There is no checksum.

Lexus UX.note: The frame is 256 bits. The data and extra words hold its 128-bit code: bits 53 to 198 without the 1 that begins every byte, the first 64 in the data word, the last 64 in the extra word. The ID (the Serial column), the button (bits 49 to 52), the head and the CRC-16 are outside the words; [the page above](lexus_ux.md#frame-256-bits) has the whole frame.

fields.name: Code, first half
fields.note: changes with every press

Ford V1 (JLR).note: KAT's serial is bytes 3–6 of the frame: `26`, the flags byte and the folded ID, so a repeat (flags `08`) shows a second serial. The button and the counter are inside the 8 encrypted bytes (Extra), and KAT shows 0 for both. [The page above](ford_v1_jlr.md#frame) has the frame byte by byte.

fields.name: Header
fields.note: `D3950E26`, as in Ford's own frames

fields.name: Flags
fields.note: `00` the first send of a press, `08` the same press again

fields.name: Folded ID
fields.note: the fob's transponder ID, high half XOR low half

fields.name: Encrypted
fields.note: button and counter inside; every byte changes with every press
